held_native_checkpoint.admission: Same real owner, PCI adapter, captured RAM and held generation; short/unlatched/stale requests reject. Existing pending generation and closed firmware writer gate remain unchanged.
held_native_checkpoint.pixels: Kernel read lease keeps pitch*height capture immutable. Native commit copies visible rows into the real leased tight SYSTEM shadow; no post-firmware VRAM read. Real native recovery precedes full-pitch pixel restoration.
held_native_checkpoint.lifetime: Abort and old-preserved retain the original hold. Native confirmed/lost retains its boot snapshot. Hardware recovery, pixels and queue quiescence latch separately; cleanup retries do not replay acknowledged recovery. Outer display ownership survives even after the native bridge has been released. Terminal transitions never reopen writers.
held_native_checkpoint.cancellation: Old-preserved means native candidate cleanup finished, even when original hold still sets retained=1. Output-lost retries abort with its exact token; failed preparation exposes retained cleanup. Virtio shutdown also retries when backend state already says bootfb. A previous native reply plus current bootfb means automatic recovery fully retired the bridge; VIRTGPU then clears its stale local receipt without calling an absent token. Only a retained cancellation reply requires abort cleanup after bootfb.
held_native_checkpoint.concurrency: Reentrant wait-spanning native UnwindGuard serializes APIs and display callbacks across driver tasks; atomic retained-owner query. Boot bridge uses its own nonblocking lifetime admission; native release enters that guard separately. No no-sleep owner spans callbacks or queue waits.
held_native_checkpoint.abi: Controlled v1 capacity-based baseline refresh; only GfxDriverDisplayApi changed. Old 56-byte field layout/signatures unchanged, size default64, prepare_held at56. Full old40/56 canaries and truncated63 checked. DriverApi35/648 and v28 query unchanged.

initial_upload_checkpoint.admission: Prepared published image and real imported shadow; no active Window image. Exact source mapping, epoch, FIFO, target Use, GPU-read lease and encoded transfer are revalidated by the real Device gate before PUT.
initial_upload_checkpoint.ownership: Normal shadow import survives creator close. DMA backing lease spans only the logical 5200 bytes in the model, including its final 1104-byte segment. RM maps the actual backing pages. A normal import never requests the page-rounded common virtual-mapping lease; queued mapping-only aliases retain their existing path. GPU execution uses a separate exact-length read lease.
initial_upload_checkpoint.transfer: One full-image 2D CE upload with distinct tight SYSTEM and aligned VRAM pitches. Only SYS semaphore completion releases the initial read use and records initial_point. It never creates a common queue job or fence.
initial_upload_checkpoint.ordering: Window/Core image submission and actual MMIO admission require initial completion for a registered presentation. Actual active image confirmation still requires Core FINISHED plus Window BEGUN. Queued frames then reuse the initial source mapping.
initial_upload_checkpoint.failure: Pre-PUT timeout can release the initial read and retry using the existing mapping. Source-acquire rejection returns an explicit retryable initial failure. Post-PUT timeout, RC fault, or failed read-release retains state and storage; an observed RC fault takes priority over simultaneous completion. Failed mapping imports retain partial references in the runtime slot.

boot_mode_checkpoint.commands: 128-word worst-mask original-header vector verifies window ownership, Head raster/min-frame-idle/viewports, exact Hz plus 1000/1001 bit in current/max clock, RM clock ownership, displayId and SOR routing. Initial RGB/identity state explicitly disables cursor/OLUT DMA references, output CSC and dithering; captured old DMA handles are never replayed into the new RAMHT.
boot_mode_checkpoint.integration: Runtime.commitBootDisplayImage derives the plan from its actual retained Device capture and catalog, then uses the existing paired Window/Core job. Device admission rederives epoch/held generation/receiver receipt/signal/image dimensions before MMIO. Final paired-notifier completion rechecks the plan before publishing it with ActiveDisplayImage; same-size later images retain that timing record.

position_checkpoint.discovery: C67B support comes only from the acknowledged RM class response. The retained WIMM channel requires its actual same-index Window and Core. No WIMM notifier or RAMHT DMA context is invented.
position_checkpoint.addressing: Compact software slots9..16 are independent of hardware channels33..40. WIMM user registers start at0x6b0000; control0x610564 and status0x6106e4. Original GA102 WINIM masks use four MP-state bits, unlike the Window stages.
position_checkpoint.commands: Typed signed16-bit X/Y SET_POINT_OUT establishes both eye positions. WIMM UPDATE interlocks with Window; Window UPDATE bit12 reciprocates, retaining its Core interlock. Boot adoption selects0,0 and the unchanged captured mode.
position_checkpoint.completion: Bounded worker submits WIMM, Window, Core in that order. Core FINISHED plus Window BEGUN must precede final coherent WIMM GET/PUT observation. GET alone cannot finish or publish position. Delayed GET retains the previous complete ActiveDisplayImage; same-size image-only commits preserve the prior position proof.
position_checkpoint.admission: Every MMIO step checks actual channel/root/held epoch, matching window index, current RM output generation, reciprocal interlock, typed stored packet and fixed deadline. A submitted position cannot be changed between channel submissions. Full-image initial CE and subsequent common Present reuse remain integrated.
position_checkpoint.lifetime: WIMM must physically retire before its Window and Core. Original register fields reject allocation, connection, pending accesses, method execution and MP activity; all-ones reads reject. Late timeout or fatal event retains all dependent rings/notifiers/images; fatal events take priority over simultaneously drainable GET. Failure diagnosis records position phase/sequence.

hdmi_checkpoint.after_scanout: After Core FINISHED, Window BEGUN and final WIMM GET: RGB8/full-range AVI with no inferred CTA VIC/aspect, preserved legacy HDMI VIC1..4 VSI or explicit VSI disable, explicit HDR packet disable, then GCP clear-AVMUTE. Head derives from the real display ID, never a fabricated PSR-head override.
hdmi_checkpoint.completion: All seven HDMI controls, or two DVI controls plus the paired scanout completion, precede ActiveDisplayImage publication. Same-size image-only commits retain the completed link receipt. A fatal event queued after final ACK still wins before publication.
hdmi_checkpoint.receiver: HF-VSDB SCDC and low-rate scrambling are independent R4GFX Report facts. A malformed extension rolls them back. Only valid complete current EDID supplies RM caps and maximum TMDS; missing/incomplete EDID supplies zero capabilities. The original captured transport-enable bit distinguishes HDMI from DVI on an HDMI socket.
hdmi_checkpoint.limits: Captured progressive RGB8 TMDS only; exact rational 1000/1001 clock comparisons. Driver ceiling600MHz HDMI/165MHz DVI plus actual advertised maximum when known. Above340MHz requires proven SCDC and high-rate support. No invented FRL, DSC, audio playback, newly advertised mode or hardware qualification.
hdmi_checkpoint.admission: One retained work/request on the canonical Runtime Exchange, exact actual display object, output/held generation, packet bytes, operation/order, phase and deadline. Setter replies are consumed only by this work. Wrong payload/owner/deadline or changed catalog rejects. No allocation or arbitrary RPC/MMIO API is added.
hdmi_checkpoint.failure: RM rejection, timeout, stale generation, failed ACK or fatal event retains rings/notifiers/images and the pending receipt where applicable. Successful earlier HDMI writes do not imply restored firmware output or physical GPU quiescence. Diagnostics retain operation, phase, ACK count, last receipt and RM/RPC status.

native_product_checkpoint.mode: Explicit OPTION NVIDIA mode=native; checks full optional prepare_held API before firmware execution. Shared serialized Device worker advances one bounded operation, finite phase/total deadlines and no synchronous wait for its own completion.
native_product_checkpoint.resources: Discover actual CE engine/context and display classes/masks. Create methods, copy channel, instance, notifiers, contiguous scanout, RAMHT upload, Core/Window/WIMM and a tight SYSTEM shadow. No prebuilt test handles enter the product owner.
native_product_checkpoint.pixels: Copy at most 64 KB of visible captured-RAM rows per worker step, excluding boot pitch padding. Both initial upload and common commit use that same immutable capture; common callback validates already completed hardware work without waiting on its own worker.
native_product_checkpoint.handoff: Matching epoch, held boot generation, receiver receipt, saved mode, actual CE SYS semaphore, WIMM GET, Window/Core notifiers and final HDMI ACK precede common software-native receipt. Later rectangles use the existing common Present consumer.
native_product_checkpoint.catalog: Same R4D may promote only its own receiver metadata port. Receiver refresh/close preserves the native binding and other ports remain visible. UNKNOWN with one saved geometry is admitted only by held-native; no connected receiver or EDID capability is invented. Ordinary prepare rejects it.
native_product_checkpoint.failure: Prepare rejection, stale receiver generation, initial CE timeout, late GCP rejection and invalid common receipt withdraw metadata while retaining reachable storage and callbacks. First status survives withdrawal. Native close follows actual advancing recovery generations; unimplemented physical restore explicitly refuses and preserves the captured RAM.

mode_control_checkpoint.integration: The real product owner waits for query completion/unwind before creating the display instance, notifiers, scanout or shadow. Actual common takeover additionally verifies the admitted result still matches. Concurrent copy/display operations cannot overlap the control Exchange.
